evals.prompt: Umbraco 17 site. I need a nightly job (an IHostedService with a timer is fine) that collects the 5 most recently published articles under the 'News' page and logs their names and URLs. I tried injecting IUmbracoContextAccessor but TryGetUmbracoContext always returns false in the job. How should I do this?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that a hosted service has no request and therefore no UmbracoContext, registers the job as a singleton that injects IUmbracoContextFactory, opens a context with EnsureUmbracoContext() inside a using for each run, and reads the published cache rather than IContentService.
expectations: The agent explains that IUmbracoContextAccessor finds nothing because a background job runs outside any HTTP request
The solution injects IUmbracoContextFactory and calls EnsureUmbracoContext() inside a using (or using declaration) for each run, not once in the constructor
Content is read from the published cache (UmbracoContext.Content or navigation services), not from IContentService
The job does not inject IPublishedContentQuery or UmbracoHelper into the singleton hosted service
The UmbracoContext or IPublishedContent read from it is not stored in a field between runs
If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the job was compiled or run

evals.prompt: On our Umbraco 17 site I'm adding a small read-only API endpoint, GET /api/products, that returns the name and price of every published product page. My plan is to inject IContentService into the controller and call GetPagedChildren on the products folder. Good plan?
evals.expected_output: The agent advises against IContentService for reads because it queries the database on every call and includes unpublished data, and implements the endpoint with the published cache (IPublishedContentQuery or IUmbracoContextFactory plus navigation services).
expectations: The agent says IContentService is the wrong choice for this read-only endpoint
The agent explains that IContentService queries the database on each call (and can return unpublished content), while the published cache is in memory
The implementation reads products through IPublishedContentQuery, UmbracoHelper, or IUmbracoContextFactory with the published cache
Only published content is returned (no explicit filtering of drafts needed because the cache holds published content)
If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the endpoint was compiled or tested

evals.prompt: I wrote a SiteService for our Umbraco 17 site that finds the contact page and the news section. It takes UmbracoHelper in its constructor and I registered it with builder.Services.AddSingleton<ISiteService, SiteService>() in a composer. Now the site won't start in Development: 'Cannot consume scoped service UmbracoHelper from singleton ISiteService'. In production it starts fine. What's wrong, and which fix is right if I also want to call the service from a scheduled job later?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains the lifetime mismatch (UmbracoHelper is scoped), notes that production only hides the bug because scope validation is off, and recommends a singleton using IUmbracoContextFactory (and navigation services) since the service must also run outside requests, rather than simply switching to AddScoped.
expectations: The agent identifies that UmbracoHelper is scoped and cannot be injected into a singleton
The agent explains that production starting fine does not mean it is safe: scope validation is off there, so the singleton would reuse one request's helper
The agent notes that AddScoped alone fixes request-only use but would not work from a scheduled job
The recommended fix for request and background use is a singleton that injects IUmbracoContextFactory and opens a context with EnsureUmbracoContext() per call
The service is registered in a composer with a lifetime that matches its dependencies
If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the fix was compiled or run

evals.prompt: Umbraco 17. Several templates and two controllers need 'the news section under the site root'. A colleague says write a static helper class with a static UmbracoHelper field, another says make a service. What's the right way, and show me the code?
evals.expected_output: The agent rejects the static UmbracoHelper field, then chooses between an extension method on IPublishedContentQuery/UmbracoHelper (small stateless lookup) and a registered custom service, and shows how it is called from a controller and a view.
expectations: The agent rejects storing UmbracoHelper in a static field because it is request-scoped
The agent offers an extension method on IPublishedContentQuery or UmbracoHelper as a valid option for a small stateless lookup
If a service is proposed, it is registered in an IComposer with a lifetime matching its dependencies
The agent shows how to call it from a controller (constructor injection) and from a view (@inject or the extension method)
The lookup null-checks the result instead of assuming the news section exists
If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the code was compiled or run

evals.prompt: Our Umbraco 17 site needs to answer 410 Gone for pages editors unpublish. Step one: whenever a page is unpublished, store the URL it had so a content finder can match it later. Write the notification handler and its registration.
evals.expected_output: The agent handles ContentUnpublishingNotification (not ContentUnpublishedNotification), reads the URL from the published cache through IUmbracoContextFactory before the page leaves it, registers the handler in a composer, and links the Umbraco 17 docs.
expectations: The handler subscribes to ContentUnpublishingNotification, not ContentUnpublishedNotification
The agent explains that the pre-notification runs before the page leaves the published cache, so its URL can still be read
The URL is read from the published cache via IUmbracoContextFactory.EnsureUmbracoContext() inside a using
The handler is registered with builder.AddNotificationHandler in an IComposer
Any Umbraco docs links point at the 17.latest pages, not the unversioned (v18) pages
If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the handler was compiled or run
